groups.decision_problem: When the required object is visible at the first inspected location, decide to acquire it immediately and move directly to the next required location (desklamp for examine tasks or destination receptacle for pick-and-place) without additional exploratory steps.
groups.shared_basis: P1:1 observes alarmclock 2 at desk 1, P1:2 takes it, P1:3 moves to dresser 1 where desklamp 1 is visible, and P1:4 uses desklamp 1. P2:1 observes cd 1 at desk 1, P2:2 takes it, P2:3 moves to shelf 1 where desklamp 1 is visible, and P2:4 uses desklamp 1. P4:1 observes pillow 1 at bed 1, P4:2 takes it, P4:3 moves to desk 1 where desklamp 1 is visible, and P4:4 uses desklamp 1. P9:1 observes soapbar 2 at countertop 1, P9:2 takes it, P9:3 moves to garbagecan 1, and P9:4 moves soapbar 2 to garbagecan 1. In all four runs, the target is acquired at the first inspected location and the next observed step completes the task without an intervening failed search.
important_differences: P1, P2, and P4 are examine-under-desklamp tasks whose completion action is use desklamp 1; P9 is a pick-and-place task whose completion action is move soapbar 2 to garbagecan 1.
The desklamp location differs: dresser 1 in P1, shelf 1 in P2, and desk 1 in P4, which changes the navigation step after acquisition.
The target object and its first-location surface differ: alarmclock 2 on desk 1 in P1, cd 1 on desk 1 in P2, pillow 1 on bed 1 in P4, and soapbar 2 on countertop 1 in P9.

groups.decision_problem: After a required item is missing from the first inspected candidate location(s), search across open surfaces or furniture and decide whether to revisit an already inspected location or move to a new one before completing the task.
groups.shared_basis: P3:1 observes cd 1 at desk 1 and P3:2 takes it; then P3:3 goes to desk 2, P3:4 goes to shelf 1, P3:5 revisits desk 1, P3:6 goes to shelf 2 where desklamp 1 is visible, and P3:7 uses desklamp 1. P7:1 goes to coffeetable 1 without finding the newspaper, P7:2-P7:7 search sidetable 1 and shelves 1-5, P7:8 revisits coffeetable 1, P7:9 goes to armchair 1 where newspaper 4 is visible, P7:10 takes newspaper 4, P7:11 goes to sofa 1, and P7:12 moves newspaper 4 to sofa 1. Both runs search multiple open locations, revisit a previously inspected location, then succeed.
important_differences: P3 is an examine-under-desklamp task and the missing item is the desklamp after the target cd 1 was already acquired; P7 is a pick-and-place task and the missing item is the target newspaper itself.
P3 revisits desk 1, the same location where it acquired the target, and then finds the desklamp at shelf 2; P7 revisits coffeetable 1 and then finds the newspaper at armchair 1.
P3 acquires the target before the extended search for the completion tool; P7 acquires the target only after the extended search.

groups.decision_problem: When the required object or tool is not visible on open surfaces, decide to open closed drawers, search through them, and decide whether to repeat the same drawer sequence or switch to other furniture before completing the task.
groups.shared_basis: P5:1-P5:6 opens and checks drawers 1-3 and finds them empty, P5:7-P5:15 checks shelves 1-9, P5:16 arrives at dresser 1 where statue 1 and desklamp 1 are visible, P5:17 takes statue 1, and P5:18 uses desklamp 1. P6:1-P6:13 searches desk 1 and opens drawers 1-6, P6:14-P6:44 repeatedly cycles through drawers 1-6, P6:45-P6:48 finds and takes cellphone 1 at sidetable 1 and moves it to shelf 1. P8:1-P8:6 searches desk 1 and opens drawers 2-3, P8:7-P8:11 repeats checks of drawers 1-3, P8:12-P8:15 finds and takes pencil 3 at shelf 1 and moves it to desk 1. P10:1-P10:10 opens drawers 1-6 sequentially, P10:11-P10:14 finds and takes statue 1 at sidetable 1 and moves it to coffeetable 1. All four runs open closed drawers during search and eventually complete the task at another location.
important_differences: P6 repeats the full drawer 1-6 cycle multiple times from P6:14 to P6:44 before moving to sidetable 1, producing a much longer search than the other runs; P8 repeats only drawers 1-3, while P10 opens drawers 1-6 in one pass and then switches to sidetable 1.

P5 is an examine-under-desklamp task and searches drawers and shelves before finding both the target statue and the desklamp together at dresser 1; P6, P8, and P10 are pick-and-place tasks and find the target on open surfaces (sidetable 1 in P6 and P10, shelf 1 in P8).
P5 opens only drawers 1-3 before checking many shelves, whereas P6, P8, and P10 focus their drawer searches around desk 1 before finding the target elsewhere.
